newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Klansmen say they helped burn S.C. church.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Klansmen say they helped burn S.C. church.

text.p: Two former Ku Klux Klan members have pleaded guilty to helping two other Klansmen burn down a black church in rural Bloomville, South Carolina, court officials said Tuesday.

The June 1995 attack on the Macedonia Baptist Church, which has since been rebuilt, was one of a rash of torchings of churches with black congregations across the southeast United States in the past few years.
Arthur Haley, 51, and Hubert "Herbert" Rowell, 50, also pleaded guilty Monday to conspiring to burn down a migrant labour camp in February 1995.
In return for the guilty pleas, prosecutors dropped 16 other charges against them.
"I hope these men can use this plea as a milestone for the day they turned away from hate," U.S. Attorney Rene Josey said.
They have since left the Klan, a white supremacist group which dates back to the post-Civil War era.
Two other Klan members, Gary Cox and Timothy Welch, pleaded guilty in August to setting the church ablaze. They are in jail awaiting sentencing.
Police said that before the burning, the Klan held a meeting in a field outside the church and chanted racial slurs at the congregation. Later a notice for a Klan rally was posted on the door.
The minister complained to police, and the church was torched a few days later.
More than 50 churches have been burned across the southeast in the past two years, but there have been no incidents for several months.
According to federal sentencing guidelines, Haley and Rowell could face 60 years in prison and a $1 million fine.
